response.sql:
WITH major_counts AS (
    SELECT m.link_to_major AS major_id,
           ma.department,
           COUNT(*) AS member_count
    FROM member AS m
    JOIN major AS ma ON m.link_to_major = ma.major_id
    GROUP BY m.link_to_major, ma.department
), major_shares AS (
    SELECT major_id,
           department,
           member_count,
           1.0 * member_count / SUM(member_count) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS share
    FROM major_counts
), ranked AS (
    SELECT major_id,
           department,
           member_count,
           share,
           share - AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS above_department_average
    FROM major_shares
)
SELECT major_id,
       department,
       member_count,
       share,
       above_department_average
FROM ranked
WHERE above_department_average > 0
ORDER BY CASE WHEN above_department_average IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
         above_department_average DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A major’s share is its member count divided by the total matched-member count in its department. Majors with no matched members are omitted because the counts are formed from matched members.

alternatives.interpretation: If “share of the members” means the share of all members matched to any major, use the overall matched-member total as the denominator; department averages are still calculated across that department’s represented majors.
